resourceProfile.assessment: Canonical English and the complete Turkish source, glossary, review metadata, and UI context were available locally.

automatedQuality.summary: Translation review generation, queue validation, type checking, focused tests, production build, route checks, and link validation passed.

linguisticCritique.summary: A fresh Turkish critique confirmed interpolation works and found protected-name drift, a false-friend date bound and measurement label, ambiguous lead terminology, and several literal recipe translations.

competentHumanReview.summary: No competent Turkish human review was performed; corrected entries remain machine reviewed.

publicationAuthorization.summary: The owner requested correction commits, not publication or deployment.

findings.summary: Steam Engine and Wire Wizard were translated as generic phrases in navigation and calculator labels.
evidence: The translation contract protects both product names.
findings.resolution: Restored Steam Engine and Wire Wizard consistently.

findings.summary: Available by was rendered as available by an agent rather than an upper date bound.
evidence: The label describes the latest date by which an item was available.
findings.resolution: Used an explicit en geç date construction.

findings.summary: Imperial units became empire units, and electrical leads used an anatomical term.
evidence: The controls select an English-system measurement mode and describe resistance-wire leads.
findings.resolution: Used İngiliz ölçü birimleri and bağlantı teli terminology.

findings.summary: Nic base and nic strength became nice base and nice strength; flavor and target labels were also overly literal.
evidence: The fields control nicotine concentration and e-liquid ingredients.
findings.resolution: Restored nicotine, aroma, target, amount, and explicit safety terminology.

findings.summary: Export and import buttons used trade nouns rather than software actions.
evidence: The controls export and import a Wire Wizard design.
findings.resolution: Used the standard Turkish software verbs.
